docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: • My name is Brendan, an Electrical Systems Engineering student at ASU, and this will be a data sheet to showcase and record my individual efforts to the creation of the weather device outside of just the team specific work.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text:
• Our EGR 304 team project involves designing and developing an environmental monitoring system capable of measuring atmospheric pressure, temperature, humidity, and light levels. My individual contribution focuses on designing a PCB that uses a pressure sensor, operational amplifier, low-pass filter, and PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller to accurately measure and process atmospheric pressure data. This subsystem will communicate with the team's other PCBs through UART, allowing the collected measurements to be displayed on a central LCD screen and contributing to the overall functionality of the environmental monitoring system.

  • My pressure-sensing subsystem is one of four PCBs that make up our environmental monitoring system. While my individual work focuses on measuring and processing atmospheric pressure, the other subsystems measure light and humidity and display the collected data. For a more in depth explanation of the system's design, objectives, and integration, visit our Team Report. team report.

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text:
My contribution to the weather sensing device is the pressure sensor. It reads absolute pressure as an analog signal, converts it into a readable digital signal, and sends it to my teammates PCB.

To review the details listed of the material used to construct the subsection, you can review it in the "BOM" section of the datasheet.

View Schematic

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This block diagram shows the main power, sensing, processing, and communication functions of the pressure-sensing PCB. The board receives 9 V power through a barrel jack, which is reduced to 5 V by a voltage regulator to provide power for the circuit. The pressure sensor produces an analog signal that is conditioned by an op amp before being sent to the PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller for processing. The microcontroller also controls an LED using a PWM-capable output to provide a visual indication of circuit operation.

The PIC communicates with the rest of the team system through Connector 1 using UART transmit and receive signals. The connector also provides a common ground connection between boards. This allows the pressure measurement collected by this PCB to be transferred to the other subsystems in the team device.

docs.title: Pin Selection Rationale
docs.text:
The RA0 pin was selected because it supports analog-to-digital conversion, allowing the PIC18F57Q43 to measure the analog voltage produced by the pressure sensor without requiring an external operational amplifier.

RC2 and RC3 were selected for UART communication between subsystems. These assignments are preliminary and will be confirmed when the team finalizes its communication interface.

The VTG and GND connections provide the microcontroller with regulated 5V power from the L7805ABV-DG voltage regulator.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This schematic illustrates the electrical design of my pressure-sensing subsystem for the EGR 304 environmental monitoring project.

The circuit incorporates a PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller, an XGZP6887A pressure sensor, an MCP6004 operational amplifier, and a 5V voltage regulator.

Additional components include a low-pass RC filter for signal conditioning, a fuse for overcurrent protection, and an 8-pin ribbon cable connector for communication between subsystems.

The pressure sensor produces an analog voltage corresponding to the measured pressure. The signal is conditioned before being processed by the PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The purpose of this power budget is to determine the electrical power requirements of my pressure-sensing subsystem and ensure that the selected voltage regulator and external power supply can safely operate all components.

The subsystem uses a Pololu 1470 power supply to provide 9V DC to an L7805ABV-DG voltage regulator, which converts the voltage to 5V. This regulated 5V supply powers the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano, CFSensor XGZP6878A15115KPA pressure sensor, and MCP6004 operational amplifier.

The MCP6004 provides analog signal conditioning, while an RC low-pass filter reduces high-frequency noise before the pressure measurement is processed by the microcontroller.

The total estimated current consumption of the major components was calculated, and a 25% safety margin was added to account for potential variations in power consumption.

docs.title: Power Budget
docs.text:
The power budget was divided into four sections:

  • Section A: Maximum current consumption of major components.
  • Section B: Power rail assignments and safety margin.
  • Section C: Voltage regulator selection and available current.
  • Section D: External power supply selection and available current.

The system operates using a single regulated 5V power rail.

docs.title: Power Budget Summary
docs.text:
Component Estimated Current PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano 20 mA CFSensor XGZP6878A15115KPA 5 mA MCP6004 Operational Amplifier 0.68 mA Curiosity Nano Support Circuitry 0.005 mA Total Current 25.685 mA 25% Safety Margin 6.421 mA Total Required Current 32.106 mA

The PIC and pressure sensor current values are provisional estimates that require verification against manufacturer specifications or physical testing. The MCP6004 current estimate represents its maximum quiescent current allowance rather than its total consumption under every possible load.

The selected L7805ABV-DG voltage regulator has a rated output current capacity of 1,500 mA, which exceeds the estimated subsystem requirement of 32.106 mA. The Pololu 1470 power supply provides 9V DC at up to 1,000 mA, offering sufficient nominal capacity for the estimated load.

Based on these calculations, the selected power components provide adequate current capacity for the pressure-sensing subsystem, subject to verification of actual component loads and regulator thermal performance.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The power budget indicates that the selected power supply and voltage regulator have sufficient current capacity to operate the pressure-sensing subsystem, including the PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller, CFSensor XGZP6878A15115KPA pressure sensor, and MCP6004 operational amplifier.

The estimated total current consumption is 25.685 mA, with a total required current of 32.106 mA after including the 25% safety margin.

The L7805ABV-DG voltage regulator is rated to supply up to 1500 mA, which exceeds the subsystem's estimated requirements.

The Pololu 1470 power supply provides 9V at a maximum of 1000 mA. Including a provisional 8 mA allowance for regulator current consumption, the estimated input current requirement is 40.106 mA. This leaves approximately 959.894 mA of available current capacity.

These calculations suggest that the selected components are suitable for the subsystem's power requirements. However, the maximum current consumption of the microcontroller, pressure sensor, and operational amplifier should be verified before the final design review. The voltage regulator's thermal performance should also be evaluated.
